learning_outcomes.text: The student/graduate masters the fundamental notions of technical thermodynamics and interprets thermal phenomena through the lens of this knowledge.
Knows the specific physical quantities that govern thermal phenomena.
Masters the mathematical models based on the principles and laws of thermodynamics and is capable of applying them.
Knows and uses thermodynamic diagrams (p-v, T-s) as tools for analyzing thermal phenomena.

Knows how to represent the processes occurring in the studied thermal machines and installations in diagrams and perform comparative analyses of the studied processes, highlighting the advantages and disadvantages resulting from this analysis.

Knows the functional schemes of thermal machines and installations and is able to describe their operation based on these schemes and in correlation with the representation of thermodynamic cycles in p-v, T-s diagrams.
Knows the main thermophysical properties of various thermodynamic agents and can explain why there are some restrictions in using certain agents.
Understands the particularities of real gases compared to perfect gases and the specific approaches.
Has the ability to elaborate energy balances and calculate specific thermodynamic quantities.
Uses tables, diagrams, and specialized software (CoolPack, REFPROP) for calculating thermodynamic parameters and analyzing thermal systems.
Develops and presents technical analysis papers and case studies based on experimental or theoretical data.
Calculates efficiencies and performance coefficients for thermal machines and installations.
Identifies technical solutions for optimizing the energy efficiency of thermal installations.
Is capable of developing professional projects of medium complexity in the field of thermal engineering.
Selects and analyzes specific bibliographic sources in the field of mechanical engineering.
Demonstrates autonomy in learning on specific mechanical engineering issues.

Respects the principles, norms, and ethical values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the work group and applies effective relationship and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously informs and documents themselves in their field of activity by adequately using effective lifelong learning methods and techniques.

syllabus_topics: Introduction notions (History, object, methods, thermodynamic systems, thermodynamic state, thermodynamic parameters, thermodynamic coefficients, thermodynamic equilibrium, concept of thermodynamic process, reversible and irreversible processes)

First Principle of Thermodynamics (Forms of energy used in technical thermodynamics, statements of the first principle of thermodynamics, Principle I in the form of equivalence, Principle I for open transformations, Principle I for open systems)

Second Principle of Thermodynamics (Applicability limits of the first principle, thermodynamic cycles, balance equation of a cycle, performance indices of direct and inverse cycles, Carnot cycle, statements of Principle II, Entropy, Principle II for reversible transformations, entropy variation in open transformations of perfect gases, Principle II for irreversible transformations, entropy of isolated systems)
Perfect gases and mixtures of perfect gases (Definition of perfect gases, laws of perfect gases, specific heats, mixtures of perfect gases, simple transformations of perfect gases)

Cycles of thermal machines and installations with perfect gas as working fluid (Generalities, cycles of piston internal combustion engines, cycles of volumetric compressors, cycles of gas turbine installations)

Real gases (Deviations of real gases from the laws of perfect gases, Andrews' isotherms, Amagat's diagram, throttling and Joule-Thomson effect, Van der Waals equation, graphical representation of Van der Waals isotherms, law of corresponding states)
Units of measurement. International System. Expression of absolute pressure.
teaching_methods: Learning by discovery through direct and indirect exploration of reality (experiment, demonstration, modeling)
assessment_rules: To pass the 'Termotehnică' course, the student must demonstrate knowledge and the ability to apply the fundamental principles of thermodynamics, especially the first and second principles, be able to characterize thermodynamic processes and cycles, the behavior of perfect and real gases, and to perform elementary energy balances for closed and open systems. The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of the corresponding study credits.
